record.title: Changes in the SUSPPUP ratio and fractional excretion of strong monovalent electrolytes in hospitalized dogs with canine babesiosis.
record.abstract: In this study an increased SUSPPUP ratio and fractional excretion of potassium in dogs infected with Babesia canis suggested mineralocorticoid excess in canine babesiosis. A significant increase in strong monovalent electrolyte fractional excretions in azotaemic dogs infected with B. canis probably resulted from acute tubular necrosis.

screening.species: B. canis (infected dogs; method not stated in abstract)
screening.rationale: Reports the SUSPPUP ratio and fractional excretion of electrolytes in hospitalised dogs. It suggests mineralocorticoid excess and tubular necrosis in azotaemic dogs.
